# Feature: Command Registry

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-062
**Source Plan**: `.spec-lite/plan_ui.md`

Every Yantra command and subcommand becomes **declarative data** in `@yantra/protocol`: its path,
arguments, options (type, input kind, default, precedence chain, applicability, help), execution
class, effect, danger, option relations, exit codes and `--json` result reference. The CLI's
commander tree is **generated from that data**, command by command, with handlers bound by path, and
`--help` stays byte-identical. A `CommandInvocation` contract with `parse` and shell-aware `format`
(POSIX, PowerShell, cmd) gives every later surface one way to describe, validate and display a
command.

Why it matters to the user:

- **The app can never drift from the CLI.** The composer (FEAT-067), the palette and generated
  surfaces (FEAT-070), the host's read RPCs and launch path (FEAT-065) and the worker adapters
  (FEAT-072) all read one registry. A flag added to the CLI is, by construction, a flag the app
  knows about (memory → General, CLI ↔ app parity).
- **"Copy as command" is trustworthy.** A command shown in the app pastes and runs correctly in
  bash, PowerShell 5.1 and cmd, or the app says plainly why cmd cannot represent it.
- **The terminal does not change.** Byte-identical `--help` and identical parse behavior are the
  acceptance bar. The one exception, known dead controls, is flagged below for a decision.

Plan acceptance (§12, FEAT-062):

- `--help` is byte-identical for every command.
- `format(parse(argv))` round-trips for every command.
- Copied commands execute correctly in bash, PowerShell 5.1 and cmd, or cmd is marked unavailable
  with the reason.
- Every command has an execution class.
- No command registers an option it cannot act on; a test asserts a consumer per option. See the
  DEVIATION below.
- Unmigrated commands appear only on a dated allowlist that FEAT-070 empties.

Milestones (plan §8): **TASK-001 to TASK-004 are the M1 slice** (read-class entries and the
generator, which FEAT-065's read-only portion needs). TASK-005 to TASK-011 complete the registry
for M4.

> **DEVIATION (awaiting confirmation): byte-identical `--help` and "no option without a consumer"
> cannot both hold today.** The current CLI already registers options its handlers ignore, verified
> in source on 2026-11-03:
>
> - `run` and `resume` register the five agent budget flags (`--max-duration`, `--max-tokens`,
>   `--tool-timeout`, `--tool-retries`, `--confirm-timeout`) through `addAgentOptions`. `run.ts`
>   passes `budgets: {}` and `resume.ts` never reads a budget.
> - `run` and `resume` register `--no-screenshots`, which neither handler reads.
> - `run --template` is registered only to refuse (`process.exit(1)`).
> - `confirm --debug` is registered and never read.
>
> Memory (General) already records the `run`/`resume` and `run --template` cases as open. Removing
> or wiring these options changes `--help` or runtime behavior, so it is outside a byte-identical
> migration. **This spec keeps `--help` byte-identical** and puts each verified dead control on a
> dated `KNOWN_DEAD_OPTIONS` allowlist (TASK-008). The list may only shrink, and any new dead option
> fails the test. The fix is tracked in `.spec-lite/TODO.md`. If the user prefers that FEAT-062 wire
> or remove them, add a task after TASK-007 that changes the affected help goldens on purpose.

## 2. Data Model (Granular)

> `.spec-lite/data_model.md` does not exist. This feature has no database. Its "data model" is the
> set of Zod schemas in `@yantra/protocol` below, plus the CLI-side binding tables. Zod stays the
> source of truth (memory → Tech Stack). Field names on wire contracts use the protocol's
> snake_case. Registry data is authored in TypeScript as `as const` objects that satisfy the input
> types, then validated by `validateCommandRegistry()` in tests.

### Entities & Attributes

- **CommandRegistry**: the whole command surface, in root-help order.
  - `registry_version` (literal `1`): bumped on any breaking shape change. NOT NULL
  - `program` (object): `{ name: 'yantra', description }`, the root command's help-visible
    metadata. The version string stays runtime-derived in the CLI.
  - `option_groups` (OptionGroup[]): named, reusable option sets.
  - `commands` (CommandEntry[]): ordered. Order equals today's registration order in
    `apps/cli/src/index.ts`, because root `--help` lists commands in that order.

- **OptionGroup**: replaces the hand-written registrars in `agent-options.ts` and
  `browser-options.ts` as data, so a group is spelled identically everywhere (memory → General,
  composed named groups).
  - `id` (enum): `agent-model | agent-budget | agent-turn | no-llm | screenshots |
browser-selection`. UNIQUE
  - `options` (OptionSpec[]): ordered exactly as the current registrar registers them.

- **CommandEntry**: discriminated union on `kind`.
  - Common fields:
    - `id` (string): dotted path, for example `config.data-dir`. UNIQUE. Must equal
      `path.join('.')`.
    - `path` (string[]): non-empty command tokens, for example `['config', 'data-dir']`.
    - `description` (string): help-visible description.
    - `help_after` (string, optional): text added through `addHelpText('after', …)` (today only
      `do`).
    - `registration` (enum `subcommand | added`): whether the command was created with
      `parent.command(name)` (inherits parent settings such as `showHelpAfterError`) or with
      `new Command()` plus `addCommand` (does not). This is behavior, not style: `ask`, `research`
      and `do` show help after an error and the other commands do not.
  - `kind: 'group'`: a command with subcommands and no action (`config`, `secret`, `daemon`,
    `model`, `sites`, `template`, `browser`). It has no execution class.
  - `kind: 'leaf'`: an executable command. Additional fields:
    - `aliases` (string[]): for example `['discover']` on `do`. DEFAULT `[]`.
    - `arguments` (ArgumentSpec[]): ordered positionals.
    - `options` (OptionRef[]): ordered. Each is `{ group: OptionGroupId }` or an inline
      OptionSpec. Group options are inserted at the reference position, which keeps help order.
    - `execution` (ExecutionSpec): NOT NULL. The plan's "every command has an execution class".
    - `effect` (enum `none | local | external`): the maximum effect. `external` means it can contact
      websites, providers or download servers; `local` means it writes Yantra-owned state; `none`
      means read only.
    - `danger` (DangerSpec): whether a generated form must ask for explicit confirmation.
    - `relations` (Relation[]): DEFAULT `[]`.
    - `exit_codes` (ExitCodeSpec[]): the subset of `0..4` this command can return, each with its
      meaning (memory → Error Handling).
    - `json` (JsonResultSpec): what `--json` emits.

- **ArgumentSpec**:
  - `name` (string): as in commander (`run-id`, `workflow-name`).
  - `description` (string).
  - `required` (boolean): `<x>` versus `[x]`.
  - `variadic` (boolean).
  - `input` (InputKind).

- **OptionSpec**:
  - `flags` (string): the exact commander flags string, for example `-p, --params <key=value...>`.
    This is the help-visible spelling.
  - `long` (string): `--params`. UNIQUE within one command after group expansion.
  - `short` (string, optional): `-p`.
  - `attribute` (string): the commander attribute name (`params`; `llm` for `--no-llm`).
  - `value` (enum `none | required | optional`), `variadic` (boolean), `negatable` (boolean, for
    `--no-x`), `repeatable` (boolean: the CLI attaches its `collect` parser).
  - `description` (string): help-visible text.
  - `default` (JSON value, optional): the **commander parse default** that help shows as
    `(default: …)`, including `false`, `[]` and string defaults such as `"3"`. Absent means no
    commander default. This is not the effective default. That one is the last step of
    `precedence`.
  - `mandatory` (boolean): registered with `requiredOption`.
  - `input` (InputKind).
  - `precedence` (PrecedenceStep[], optional): how the effective value resolves, in order. For
    example `--model`: `flag → env YANTRA_AGENT_MODEL → preference agent.model → default`.
  - `applicability` (Condition[], optional): when the option has an effect. For example
    `--turn-timeout` applies only on the LLM path, and `--detail` only to terminal output.
  - `danger` (DangerSpec, optional): option-level danger, such as `--force` or `init --reset`.

- **InputKind**: discriminated on `kind`. These are the plan's form-metadata kinds.
  - `text`, `bool`, `duration`, `workflow-ref`, `template-ref`, `run-ref`, `secret-input`.
  - `enum`: `{ choices: string[], enforced_by: 'parser' | 'handler' }`. Only `parser` choices
    become commander `.choices()`, which affects help (`(choices: …)`) and parse errors. `prefs`'
    `action` is validated by its handler today, so it is `handler`.
  - `number`: `{ integer: boolean, min?: number }`.
  - `path`: `{ target: 'file' | 'dir' }`.

- **PrecedenceStep**: discriminated on `source`.
  - `flag`;
  - `env { name }`: the variable's **name** only;
  - `preference { key }` (`profile.yaml`);
  - `config { key }` (`config.yaml`);
  - `default { value, note? }`.

- **Condition**: one of:
  - `{ option: long, present: true }`;
  - `{ option: long, equals: JSON value }`;
  - `{ argument: name, in: string[] }`;
  - `{ mode: 'llm' | 'deterministic' }`.

- **ExecutionSpec**:
  - `default` (ExecutionClass).
  - `rules` (`{ when: Condition, class: ExecutionClass }[]`): the first match wins. For example,
    `doctor` is `read` by default and `run` when `--agent-smoke` is present. `prefs` is `mutate`
    when `action ∈ {set, approve}` or `--forget` is present, and `read` otherwise.
  - `adapter` (`{ id, executes_as?: ExecutionClass, note }`, optional): required when the class is
    `adapter`. The ids are `init-onboarding`, `open-result-view`, `config-edit-yaml`,
    `daemon-control` and `confirm-inbox`.
  - `exemption` (`{ decision: string, reason }`, optional): required when the class is
    `exemption`. For example `config data-dir` → `D15`.
- **ExecutionClass** (enum): `run | read | mutate | exclusive | in-process-secure | adapter |
exemption`. These are the plan §6 classes.
- **DangerSpec**: `{ level: 'none' } | { level: 'confirm', reason }`.
- **Relation**: `{ kind: 'requires' | 'conflicts', option: long, with: long[], note? }`. Declare
  only relations the CLI already enforces, since the registry describes behavior and does not
  invent it.
- **ExitCodeSpec**: `{ code: 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4, meaning }`.
- **JsonResultSpec**:
  - `flag` (`'--json' | null`);
  - `shape` (`document | ndjson | envelope | none`);
  - `schema` (string | null): the exported protocol schema name, for example `Brief` or
    `TaskEvent`. `null` means "not yet described"; FEAT-065 and FEAT-066 fill these in for the read
    RPCs they serve.

- **CommandInvocation**: a wire contract (plan §6, D13), what was **requested**.
  - `invocation_id` (string): ULID (`ULID_PATTERN`). Client-generated idempotency key (D11).
  - `path` (string[]): the **canonical** command path, with aliases resolved (`discover` → `do`).
  - `argv` (string[]): the tokens after the path, exactly as given, in order.
  - `cwd` (string): absolute. NOT NULL (D13: app invocations always carry it).

- **ParsedInvocation** (in memory, not persisted):
  - `invocation` (CommandInvocation) and `entry` (the leaf CommandEntry);
  - `arguments` (`Record<name, string | string[]>`);
  - `options` (`Record<attribute, JSON value>`): with commander defaults applied, matching
    commander's `opts()`;
  - `explicit` (string[]): attributes the user actually set. FEAT-067's effective-value sources and
    D13's "pin as explicit flags" need this.
  - `execution` (ExecutionClass): the result of `executionClassFor(entry, parsed)`.

- **ParseError** (`Result` error branch, never thrown):
  - `code` (enum): `unknown_command | group_requires_subcommand | unknown_option |
missing_option_value | missing_argument | too_many_arguments | invalid_choice |
missing_required_option | help_or_version`;
  - `message` (string): CLI vocabulary;
  - `token_index` (number, optional);
  - `suggestion` (string, optional).

- **FormatResult**: `{ ok: true, text } | { ok: false, reason: 'shell_unrepresentable' |
'secret_input', detail }`.
- **Shell** (enum): `posix | powershell | cmd`.

### Relationships

- CommandRegistry 1:N CommandEntry, and 1:N OptionGroup.
- A leaf CommandEntry N:M OptionGroup, through `OptionRef { group }`. A group's options expand in
  place.
- A CommandInvocation N:1 leaf CommandEntry, by `path`.
- CLI side: a leaf CommandEntry 1:1 handler, through `HANDLERS: Record<LeafCommandId, Handler>` in
  `apps/cli/src/registry/handlers.ts`. The `satisfies` constraint makes a missing handler a
  `src` typecheck error, which `tsc` enforces because `src` is in the package's `include`.

### Indexes & Constraints

`validateCommandRegistry()` enforces these. A failure throws `CommandRegistryError`, an `Error`
subclass naming the entry and the rule.

- `id` and `path` are unique, and `id === path.join('.')`.
- Every non-root path prefix is a `group` entry, and groups have at least one child.
- After group expansion, `long`, `short` and `attribute` are unique within a command.
- Every leaf has `execution`. Class `adapter` requires `adapter`, and `exemption` requires
  `exemption`.
- Every `Condition` and `Relation` names an option or argument that exists on that command.
- `default` agrees with `input` and `value`: booleans for `value: none`, arrays for `repeatable`, and
  enum defaults within `choices`.
- `json.flag === '--json'` exactly when the command registers `--json`.
- `exit_codes` is non-empty and always includes `0`.
- `aliases` do not collide with any sibling name or alias.
- The registry modules import no Node built-ins and nothing outside `src/commands/`. A boundary
  test checks this so browser consumers can import them.

## 3. Files

**Protocol (`packages/protocol`)**

- `src/commands/schema.ts`: Zod schemas for every entity above, with `.describe()` text that feeds
  the generated protocol docs.
- `src/commands/validate.ts`: `validateCommandRegistry()` and `CommandRegistryError`.
- `src/commands/execution.ts`: `executionClassFor(entry, parsed)`.
- `src/commands/groups.ts`: the `OptionGroup` data, moved from the CLI registrars.
- `src/commands/entries/*.ts`: entry data by family:
  - `agentic.ts`: `ask`, `research`, `do`;
  - `workflow.ts`: `run`, `resume`, `confirm`, `lint`, `schedule`, `schedules`, `unschedule`;
  - `settings.ts`: `config`, `secret`, `model`, `prefs`, `profile`, `sites`, `init`;
  - `runs.ts`: `list`, `show`, `open`, `usage`, `audit`, `report`;
  - `template.ts`, `daemon.ts`, `doctor.ts`, `browser.ts`.
- `src/commands/registry.ts`: `COMMAND_REGISTRY`, assembled in root-help order. Also
  `LeafCommandId` and `findCommand(path)`.
- `src/commands/invocation.ts`: the `CommandInvocation` schema, `parseInvocation()` and
  `createInvocationId()`, which wraps `generateUlid`.
- `src/commands/format.ts`: `formatInvocation(invocation, shell, { program? })` and
  `defaultShellFor(platform)`.
- `src/commands/index.ts`: the browser-safe barrel.
- `src/index.ts` (modify): re-export the barrel.
- `package.json` (modify): add the subpath export `./commands` → `dist/commands/index.js`.
- `src/emit/json-schema.ts` (modify): add `command-invocation.json` and `command-registry.json`.
- `generated/json-schema/command-invocation.json`, `generated/json-schema/command-registry.json`:
  emitted, never hand-edited.
- `scripts/verify-exports.ts` (modify): allowlist the symbols the CLI does not consume yet
  (`formatInvocation`, `defaultShellFor`, `parseInvocation`, `createInvocationId`), with
  `FEAT-065` and `FEAT-070` as owners.
- Tests:
  - `tests/commands/schema.spec.ts`: schemas and validation;
  - `tests/commands/execution.spec.ts`;
  - `tests/commands/registry.spec.ts`: the shipped registry validates, plus the lexical danger
    guard;
  - `tests/commands/boundary.spec.ts`: no Node built-ins under `src/commands/`;
  - `tests/commands/invocation.spec.ts`;
  - `tests/commands/format.spec.ts`;
  - `tests/commands/format.property.spec.ts` (fast-check);
  - `tests/commands/shell-tokenizers.ts`: reference tokenizers used by tests only.

**CLI (`apps/cli`)**

- `src/program.ts` (new): `buildProgram(options, bindings?)`, extracted from `index.ts`'s `run()`.
  `run()` keeps the banner and exit-code mapping and calls `buildProgram`.
- `src/registry/build-command-tree.ts` (new): the commander generator. It reproduces:
  - flags, descriptions and defaults;
  - parser-enforced choices;
  - `requiredOption`;
  - the `collect` parser for repeatable options;
  - aliases;
  - `help_after`;
  - `registration` (`.command()` versus `addCommand`).
- `src/registry/handlers.ts` (new): `buildHandlers(cliRunOptions)` returns
  `Record<LeafCommandId, Handler>`. The `Handler` signature is commander-shaped
  (`(args, options, command) => Promise<void> | void`) so FEAT-072 can replace it without touching
  the generator.
- `src/registry/unmigrated.ts` (new): `UNMIGRATED_COMMANDS`, a dated allowlist of top-level
  commands still built by hand. Each entry has `{ path, since, reason, owner: 'FEAT-070' }`. The
  goal is to empty it by TASK-007.
- `src/commands/*.ts` (modify): each migrated `make*Command`/`register*Command` becomes an exported
  handler function. The business logic is unchanged. Inline commander registration is deleted.
- `src/agent-options.ts`, `src/browser-options.ts` (modify):
  - The `add*Options` registrars are replaced by group data and removed once their last caller
    migrates.
  - `resolveAgentInvocation`, `parseDuration` and `resolveBrowserSelectionOverride` stay.
- `src/template-ref.ts` (modify): `TEMPLATE_OPTION_DESCRIPTION` moves into the registry data and

- `scripts/capture-cli-surface.ts` (new): captures the goldens once, from the pre-migration tree.

- `tests/registry/cli-surface.spec.ts`: byte comparison against the goldens.
- `tests/registry/tree-agreement.spec.ts`: registry ⇄ live tree.
- `tests/registry/completeness.spec.ts`: every live path is in the registry, and every leaf has a

**End to end**

**Documentation**

- `docs/protocol-spec.md`: regenerated by `emit`, never hand-edited.

## 4. Dependencies

- **None blocking.** Plan §8 lets FEAT-062 start at once, in parallel with FEAT-061 and the spikes.
- **Downstream consumers:**
  - FEAT-072 (handler seams) starts after this feature. The `Handler` binding here is
    deliberately commander-shaped so FEAT-072 can replace it.
  - FEAT-065 needs the read-class entries (TASK-003/004) and `CommandInvocation` (TASK-009). It
    also adds the `ui` command's registry entry (class `exemption`), because `ui` does not exist
    yet and registering it here would create a dead command.
  - FEAT-067 needs `precedence`, `applicability` and `explicit`.
  - FEAT-070 needs `format`, `danger`, adapters and the `UNMIGRATED_COMMANDS` allowlist, which it
    empties.
- **No new dependencies.** It uses `zod`, `zod-to-json-schema`, `commander` (already in the CLI)
  and `fast-check` (already a dev dependency of protocol and the CLI).

### TASK-009: `CommandInvocation` and `parseInvocation`

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - In `packages/protocol/src/commands/invocation.ts`: - add the `CommandInvocation` Zod schema; - add `createInvocationId()`, which wraps `generateUlid`; - add `parseInvocation(argv: readonly string[], context: { cwd: string; invocationId?:
string; registry?: CommandRegistry }): Result<ParsedInvocation, ParseError>`.
  - The parser replicates commander 14's grammar for this registry:
    - Command resolution walks the registry from the first token and resolves aliases to canonical
      paths. A group without a subcommand gives `group_requires_subcommand`.
    - Options may appear before, between or after positionals.
    - Accepted option forms: `--opt value`, `--opt=value`, `-p value` and `-pvalue`.
    - `--no-x` negation is supported; repeatable options accumulate.
    - Variadic option values continue until the next token that starts with `-`.
    - `--` ends option parsing.
    - `-h`/`--help` and `-V`/`--version` give `help_or_version`.
    - Choices are checked only for `enforced_by: 'parser'`.
    - Error cases: missing mandatory options, missing required arguments, and excess arguments
      (commander 14 rejects them by default).
  - The result fills `options` with commander defaults applied, `explicit` with the attributes
    actually set, and `execution` through `executionClassFor`. `cwd` must be absolute, accepting a
    POSIX `/…` or a Windows `X:\…` or `\\…` form, without `node:path`.
  - Add `command-invocation.json` to the emitted schemas.

### TASK-010: Shell-aware `formatInvocation` and round-trip for every command

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - In `src/commands/format.ts`, add `formatInvocation(invocation, shell, { program = 'yantra' })`
    and `defaultShellFor(platform)`, where `win32` gives `powershell` and anything else gives
    `posix`. The output is `program`, then the canonical `path`, then `argv`; each token is quoted
    per shell:
    - **posix:** bare if the token matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_@%+=:,./-]+$`. Otherwise single-quote it,
      writing `'` as `'\''`. An empty token is `''`. Newlines are carried inside single quotes.
    - **powershell (5.1 native-argument rules):** bare only for a conservative safe set. A token
      starting with `@`, `-` followed by a non-flag character, or containing any of
      `` `$,;(){}<>|&#'" `` or whitespace is single-quoted, with `'` written as `''`.
      - Embedded `"` must survive PowerShell 5.1's legacy native-argument passing, written as
        `\"` inside the quoted token.
      - An empty token is `'""'`, because 5.1 drops a bare `''` for native commands.
      - The real-shell test (TASK-011) is the authority: these rules are the starting point and are
        adjusted to whatever the test proves.
    - **cmd:** double-quote any token containing whitespace or `&|<>()^,;=`. The format returns
      `{ ok: false, reason: 'shell_unrepresentable', detail }` with a token-specific detail when
      any token contains a newline or CR, `"`, `%` or a control character.
    - **Secret inputs:** if any argument or option with input `secret-input` has a value, return
      `{ ok: false, reason: 'secret_input' }` for **every** shell. A secret is never rendered into
      a copyable command (plan §7).
  - A `program` prefix that contains spaces is quoted per shell. PowerShell additionally uses the
    call operator `& '<path>'`.
- [ ] **Unit Tests**:
  - `format.spec.ts`: a golden table per shell for quotes, `$`, backticks, `%`, `^`, `!`,
    newline, empty string, leading `-`, `@`, unicode (`é`, `東京`), a program path with spaces,
    each cmd unavailability reason, and secret refusal.
  - `format.property.spec.ts`. For **every leaf**, it generates valid invocations from the
    registry (as in TASK-009) with argument values drawn from an adversarial alphabet. It asserts
    that `parseInvocation(tokenize(format(inv, shell)).slice(programTokens), …)` deep-equals the
    original parse. `tokenize` comes from `tests/commands/shell-tokenizers.ts`: a reference POSIX
    tokenizer, a reference PowerShell 5.1 native-argument tokenizer, and the MSVCRT
    command-line rules for cmd. This covers every shell where the format is available.

## 6. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Auth**: N/A. The registry and `CommandInvocation` carry no tokens. `secret-input` values are
  never formatted (TASK-010), and `CommandInvocation` has no field for an out-of-band secret.
  FEAT-065 keeps credential writes in-process (D2).
- **Error Handling**:
  - CLI behavior and exit codes are unchanged, and the stderr goldens (TASK-001) pin this.
  - Registry violations throw `CommandRegistryError`, an `Error` subclass with `entryId` and
    `rule` (memory → Coding Standards). They surface in tests and at CLI startup only through a
    missing-handler guard in the generator.
  - `parseInvocation` returns `Result<ParsedInvocation, ParseError>` and never throws, so the
    palette (FEAT-070) can explain an unparseable command.
  - `formatInvocation` returns a typed refusal reason instead of a best-effort string.
- **Logging**: N/A. The registry, generator, parser and formatter are pure and silent. No log line
  may ever contain a formatted invocation that has a `secret-input` value, and the formatter makes
  that structurally impossible.
- **Security**:
  - Workers are spawned shell-free from `{path, argv}` (FEAT-065). Formatting exists for display
    and Copy only.
  - `@yantra/protocol/commands` imports no Node built-ins, so the browser bundle loads no
    filesystem code.
- **Paths**: The feature builds no Yantra paths. `cwd` absoluteness is checked syntactically
  (memory → Project Structure: only `paths.ts` builds Yantra paths).
- **Product words**: Descriptions and enum values are the CLI's own strings, moved verbatim (plan
  §9).
